raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

Fixes #57342. Choose the CPU→GPU load path from the copy sizes actually submitted, not the page size.

### User case

1. Canonical offload layout (`TieringOffloadingSpec`, `canonical_layout: true`)
   with an LBNHC KV layout at TP > 1: `FLEX_ATTENTION` (its only layout) or
   `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=NHD`.
2. Llama-3.1-8B at TP=2 has a 32 KiB page per rank, so `_select_swap_blocks_fn`
   picks `cuMemcpyBatchAsync`.
3. But the canonical mapping splits each page into 16 per-token 2 KiB fragments,
   and `_fill_canonical_ops` submits one copy per fragment, which is the
   small-copy regime #42212 moved to Triton.
4. Each CPU prefix hit copies about 4x slower than it needs to: TTFT p50 88 ms
   instead of 46 ms for a 2K-token prefix on 2×A30.

The fix passes the fragment sizes to the selector and applies the existing
28 KiB threshold and 8-byte alignment check to them.

Unchanged: the direct layout, the connector's default LBHNC layout without DCP
(one run per page), stores (always DMA), and the Triton chunk size (still
page-derived).

The split K/V example in #57342 turned out not to reach the connector at
runtime, since the connector always gets the packed 4-D view.

Not a duplicate: no open PR touches the selector. Neighbours are #48936, #53971,
#53544. The threshold itself being device-dependent is tracked separately in
#57555.

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_canonical_layout.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_gpu_worker.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_canonical_mapping.py
pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/gpu_worker.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_canonical_layout.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/cpu/test_gpu_worker.py
```

The existing two-rank GPU roundtrip in `test_canonical_layout.py` gains a
32 KiB page loaded as 2 × 16 KiB fragments (must take Triton, 16 descriptors)
and an aligned page with 508 B fragments (must stay on DMA). Both must reload
byte-exact.

## Test Result

```text
78 passed on A30 (ROCm-only test deselected); the two new cases fail on main
pre-commit, incl. mypy: passed
```

Serving, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct TP=2 on 2×A30, `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=NHD`, every
measured request loads its prefix from CPU, median of 3 servers:

| case | main | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| TTFT p50, 2K prefix, c1 | 88.1 ms | 46.4 ms |
| TTFT p50, 2K prefix, c8 | 487 ms | 114 ms |
| requests/s, 2K prefix, c8 | 3.70 | 4.36 |
| TPOT, 2K prefix, c8 | 13.2 ms | 13.4 ms |
| TTFT p50, 8K prefix, c1 | 272 ms | 113 ms |

Greedy outputs are identical between main and this PR at concurrency 1
(240/240). At c8 they also differ between main servers, and this PR stays in
that range. Setup and command: [this comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57343#discussion_r4374343895).

<details>
<summary>Measurement details</summary>

- Revision: main 7342dc0317 (merge-base) vs this PR (da62d10438), with the same
  compiled extensions in both arms (08633cb5c nightly, because this box's 535
  driver can't run the CUDA 13 wheels published for 7342dc0317).
- 2× A30 24GB PCIe Gen4, torch 2.13.0+cu126, Triton 3.7.1, CUDA 12.8
  forward-compat libcuda.
- TPOT +2% at c8 is consistent across servers, likely the Triton kernel sharing
  SMs with decode (not profiled).
- Sizing the Triton chunk to the fragment was slower for 512 B fragments
  (408 ms vs 356 ms for a 32K-token load) and within 2–4% for 1–2 KiB, so it
  stays page-derived.
- The earlier standalone copy measurements are in #57342.

</details>

AI assistance (Claude) was used for investigation, code, tests and
measurements. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and measurements
on my own hardware.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

One concern is that this change still relies on a single empirically tuned , while the DMA/Triton crossover likely depends on both payload size and descriptor count.  runs at handler initialization and does not know the actual batch size N; the Triton wrapper only falls back to DMA for very small N.

In a local H100 sweep, for example, DMA was faster for 28 KiB descriptors at N=64, while Triton was faster at N=256. Similarly, the crossover for 8 KiB descriptors moved between N=16 and N=64.

Could we add a small size × descriptor-count benchmark, or document why a single 28 KiB cutoff is expected to generalize across workloads and devices? If runtime autotuning is out of scope for this PR, this seems like a good follow-up for a per-device/per-N dispatch policy. The fragment-size fix itself still makes sense.

nodes.body:
Here are the serving numbers on 2x A30. The configuration that produces fragmented canonical mappings at runtime is an LBNHC KV layout at TP > 1 (`FLEX_ATTENTION`, whose only layout is LBNHC, or `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=NHD`): each rank's 32 KiB page maps to 16 per-token 2 KiB fragments. I've updated the description to use this case instead of the split K/V example, which never reaches the connector at runtime.

Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct TP=2, FLASH_ATTN with `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=NHD`, canonical layout on `TieringOffloadingSpec`. Every measured request loads its prefix from CPU. Median of 3 servers per arm, run interleaved:

| workload | | main | this PR |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| 2K-token prefix, concurrency 1 | TTFT p50 | 88.1 ms | 46.4 ms |
| | copy time per load, per rank | 54 ms | 13 ms |
| 2K-token prefix, concurrency 8 | TTFT p50 | 487 ms | 114 ms |
| | requests/s | 3.70 | 4.36 |
| | TPOT | 13.2 ms | 13.4 ms |
| 8K-token prefix, concurrency 1 | TTFT p50 | 272 ms | 113 ms |

With `FLEX_ATTENTION` and no layout override (one server each), TTFT p50 at concurrency 1 goes from 98.8 to 56.4 ms.

TPOT rises by about 2% at concurrency 8, consistently across servers (13.18-13.22 vs 13.41-13.50 ms). My guess is that the Triton load kernel takes SMs from decode, where the DMA path uses the copy engine. I haven't profiled it.

Output verification, greedy decoding:

- Concurrency 1: all 192 (2K) and 48 (8K) completions are identical between main and this PR. For 2K they also match a server without offloading. For 8K, 38/48 match it in both arms.
- Concurrency 8: completions vary between servers on main itself (178-184/192 identical), and this PR vs main is in the same range (174-176/192).

<details>
<summary>Setup and reproduction</summary>

- Revision: main = 7342dc0317 (this PR's merge-base), this PR = da62d10438. Only `gpu_worker.py` differs between the two arms.
- Binaries: this box has a 535 kernel driver with the CUDA 12.8 forward-compat libcuda, and only CUDA 13 wheels are published for 7342dc0317. So both arms use the compiled extensions from the 08633cb5c nightly (CUDA 12). A local source build would compile out `cuMemcpyBatchAsync` (no nvcc >= 12.8 on this box) and change the DMA baseline.
- Hardware: 2x A30 24GB (PCIe Gen4, same NUMA node), 2x Xeon Gold 6342; torch 2.13.0+cu126, Triton 3.7.1.
- Workload: 64 prefixes of 2048 tokens sent once, then 192 requests cycling through them, each with a fresh 32-token suffix. The GPU cache is capped at 2048 blocks, so each prefix is evicted before it comes around again (384 loads = 192 requests x 2 ranks). Concurrency 1 with 16 output tokens, then concurrency 8 with 128. The 8K run uses 16 prefixes of 8000 tokens and 48 requests. Temperature 0, `ignore_eos`. 8 unmeasured warm-up requests keep the Triton JIT out of the numbers.
- Server:

```bash
VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=NHD vllm serve meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --attention-backend FLASH_ATTN --block-size 16 \
  --num-gpu-blocks-override 2048 --enable-prefix-caching --max-model-len 8192 \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"OffloadingConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"spec_name":"TieringOffloadingSpec","cpu_bytes_to_use":25769803776,"canonical_layout":true}}'
```

The client is a small aiohttp script; I can put it in a gist if that helps.

</details>

+def _tp2_split_kv_mapping(rank: int, half: int) -> CanonicalPageMapping:
+    # split K/V HND page, tp=2: the rank's heads are contiguous, so K and V
+    # each copy as one fragment of half the local page
+    runs = (
+        CopyRun(0, rank * half, half, 1, half, half),
+        CopyRun(half, (2 + rank) * half, half, 1, half, half),
+    )
+    return CanonicalPageMapping(4 * half, 2 * half, runs, 1, 0, True)
+
+
+def _whole_page_mapping(page: int) -> CanonicalPageMapping:
+    identity = CopyRun(0, 0, page, 1, page, page)
+    return CanonicalPageMapping(page, page, (identity,), 1, 0, True)

inline_comments.body:
Here are the serving numbers on 2x A30. The configuration that produces fragmented canonical mappings at runtime is an LBNHC KV layout at TP > 1 (`FLEX_ATTENTION`, whose only layout is LBNHC, or `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=NHD`): each rank's 32 KiB page maps to 16 per-token 2 KiB fragments. I've updated the description to use this case instead of the split K/V example, which never reaches the connector at runtime.

Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct TP=2, FLASH_ATTN with `VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=NHD`, canonical layout on `TieringOffloadingSpec`. Every measured request loads its prefix from CPU. Median of 3 servers per arm, run interleaved:

| workload | | main | this PR |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| 2K-token prefix, concurrency 1 | TTFT p50 | 88.1 ms | 46.4 ms |
| | copy time per load, per rank | 54 ms | 13 ms |
| 2K-token prefix, concurrency 8 | TTFT p50 | 487 ms | 114 ms |
| | requests/s | 3.70 | 4.36 |
| | TPOT | 13.2 ms | 13.4 ms |
| 8K-token prefix, concurrency 1 | TTFT p50 | 272 ms | 113 ms |

With `FLEX_ATTENTION` and no layout override (one server each), TTFT p50 at concurrency 1 goes from 98.8 to 56.4 ms.

TPOT rises by about 2% at concurrency 8, consistently across servers (13.18-13.22 vs 13.41-13.50 ms). My guess is that the Triton load kernel takes SMs from decode, where the DMA path uses the copy engine. I haven't profiled it.

Output verification, greedy decoding:

- Concurrency 1: all 192 (2K) and 48 (8K) completions are identical between main and this PR. For 2K they also match a server without offloading. For 8K, 38/48 match it in both arms.
- Concurrency 8: completions vary between servers on main itself (178-184/192 identical), and this PR vs main is in the same range (174-176/192).

<details>
<summary>Setup and reproduction</summary>

- Revision: main = 7342dc0317 (this PR's merge-base), this PR = da62d10438. Only `gpu_worker.py` differs between the two arms.
- Binaries: this box has a 535 kernel driver with the CUDA 12.8 forward-compat libcuda, and only CUDA 13 wheels are published for 7342dc0317. So both arms use the compiled extensions from the 08633cb5c nightly (CUDA 12). A local source build would compile out `cuMemcpyBatchAsync` (no nvcc >= 12.8 on this box) and change the DMA baseline.
- Hardware: 2x A30 24GB (PCIe Gen4, same NUMA node), 2x Xeon Gold 6342; torch 2.13.0+cu126, Triton 3.7.1.
- Workload: 64 prefixes of 2048 tokens sent once, then 192 requests cycling through them, each with a fresh 32-token suffix. The GPU cache is capped at 2048 blocks, so each prefix is evicted before it comes around again (384 loads = 192 requests x 2 ranks). Concurrency 1 with 16 output tokens, then concurrency 8 with 128. The 8K run uses 16 prefixes of 8000 tokens and 48 requests. Temperature 0, `ignore_eos`. 8 unmeasured warm-up requests keep the Triton JIT out of the numbers.
- Server:

```bash
VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=NHD vllm serve meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --attention-backend FLASH_ATTN --block-size 16 \
  --num-gpu-blocks-override 2048 --enable-prefix-caching --max-model-len 8192 \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"OffloadingConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"spec_name":"TieringOffloadingSpec","cpu_bytes_to_use":25769803776,"canonical_layout":true}}'
```

The client is a small aiohttp script; I can put it in a gist if that helps.

</details>

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

One concern is that this change still relies on a single empirically tuned , while the DMA/Triton crossover likely depends on both payload size and descriptor count.  runs at handler initialization and does not know the actual batch size N; the Triton wrapper only falls back to DMA for very small N.

In a local H100 sweep, for example, DMA was faster for 28 KiB descriptors at N=64, while Triton was faster at N=256. Similarly, the crossover for 8 KiB descriptors moved between N=16 and N=64.

Could we add a small size × descriptor-count benchmark, or document why a single 28 KiB cutoff is expected to generalize across workloads and devices? If runtime autotuning is out of scope for this PR, this seems like a good follow-up for a per-device/per-N dispatch policy. The fragment-size fix itself still makes sense.
